 Our group explores new regimes of frequency comb physics — laser sources that generate thousands of evenly spaced spectral lines, acting as ultra-precise rulers for measuring light. We study liquid-like light in fast-gain semiconductor lasers, where strong nonlinear dynamics can produce stable and controllable broadband states. Our research combines semiconductor device fabrication, precision optical […] ts, and theoretical and numerical modelling to understand and control these systems.
 Project background
 This project investigates the dynamics, fluctuations, and open-system physics of liquid light . The doctoral student will work across the full experimental cycle: developing and fabricating photonic devices, building and operating optical setups, performing precision measurements, and modelling the underlying nonlinear dynamics.
 Job description
 Designing and fabricating semiconductor photonic devices using cleanroom processes, followed by their electrical and optical characterization.
 Building and operating advanced laser and optical measurement setups to study temporal dynamics, fluctuations, coherence, and controlled light–matter interactions.
 Developing theoretical and numerical models to describe nonlinear laser dynamics, interpret experiments, and guide the design of new devices and measurements.
 The goal is to establish a versatile experimental platform for probing and controlling liquid-light dynamics, connecting device physics, precision measurements, and nonlinear photonic theory.

In the past decades, photographs and videos of events were regarded as reliable evidence for both news media and forensic investigations. However, recent developments in AI technology now make it possible, with minimal technological knowledge or skills, to create extremely convincing manipulated or synthesised images, audio and video data, often called DeepFakes.

Wir suchen eine engagierte Person zur Mitarbeit an einem Forschungsprojekt zur Untersuchung von Hautgewebe von Hunden mit spontanem und experimentell induziertem Cushing-Syndrom in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Institut für Tierpathologie der Universität Bern. Stable Diffusion) als kontrollierbare Datensatzdarstellung für Training sowie Validierung von Netzwerken für nachgelagerte Aufgaben interessiert.
 Nicht alle Datenpunkte in einem Datensatz sind gleichermaßen wichtig für die Leistung eines neuronalen Netzwerks. Mit fortschreitendem Training ist der Verlust einiger Datenpunkte möglicherweise nicht mehr […] ekräftig, da das Netzwerk bereits alles daraus gelernt hat, was es kann. Daher kann es von Vorteil sein, das Netzwerktraining zu beobachten, um die richtigen Daten zur richtigen Zeit bereitzustellen. Allerdings ist die Auswahl von Daten aus einem festen Datensatz problematisch, wenn kein Bild mit der genauen Mischung von Attributen vorhanden ist. Ziel dieses Doktorandenprojekts ist die Entwicklung neuer Lernalgorithmen zur Generierung relevanter Daten „on Demand“ als Reaktion auf den Bedarf des Netzwerks. Dazu gehört unter anderem die Verbesserung der Trainingseffizienz durch die Synthese von Daten besserer Relevanz sowie durch gezielte Erstellung von Beispielen sicherzustellen, dass die gewünschte Invarianz erzielt wird.
 Als Teil unseres Teams entwickeln Sie neuartige Ansätze zur Anpassung von Deep Generative Models (z.B. Diffusion Models, GANs, VAEs) als Datenquellen, um nachgelagerte Modelle besser zu trainieren und zu validieren.
 Darüber hinaus nutzen Sie die Steuerbarkeit und das Wissen generativer Basismodelle, um Datensätze nicht mehr nur als eine lose Sammlung von Bildern zu betrachten.

industrial:bosch:744000136168313.desc:
Bei Bosch Research treiben wir die nächste Generation von Physical AI voran: intelligente Systeme, die ihre Umgebung in der realen Welt wahrnehmen, darüber schlussfolgern und robust handeln können. Da Fahrzeuge zunehmend geteilt, automatisiert und softwaredefiniert werden, wird das Verständnis dessen, was im Fahrzeuginnenraum passiert, ebenso wichtig wie das Verständnis der Straße vor dem Fahrzeug. Die Fähigkeit, Position, Haltung und Bewegung von Insassinnen und Insassen zu erkennen, entwickelt sich sowohl zu einer regulatorischen Anforderung als auch zu einem zentralen Enabler für […]  Sicherheits- und Komfortfunktionen. Aktuelle Wahrnehmungssysteme behandeln den Fahrzeuginnenraum und die Außenumgebung jedoch weitgehend als getrennte Domänen, was ihre Fähigkeit einschränkt, aus der kleinen Anzahl an Kameras, die realistisch in einem Fahrzeug eingesetzt werden können, ein konsistentes dreidimensionales Verständnis des Innenraums zu bilden.
 In diesem Promotionsprojekt untersuchen Sie neuronale 3D-Szenenrepräsentationen, darunter Neural Radiance Fields, Gaussian Splatting und implizite Occupancy-Modelle, und passen diese an die besonderen Herausforderungen der In-Cabin-Wahrnehmung an. Anders als in Außenumgebungen, in denen ein bewegter Sensor eine weitgehend statische Szene beobachtet, stellt der Fahrzeuginnenraum das gegenteilige Szenario dar: Die Struktur ist fest und bekannt, während die Insassinnen und Insassen die primäre Bewegungsquelle sind und artikulierte, verformbare sowie kontinuierlich wechselnde Bewegungsmuster zeigen. Sie nutzen diese Asymmetrie als Vorteil, indem Sie die bekannte Innenraumgeometrie als integrierte Supervision einsetzen und moderne 3D-bewusste Diffusionsmodelle als gelernte Priors einbeziehen. Ihre Forschung konzentriert sich darauf, Insassinnen und Insassen zuverlässig aus nur ein bis drei festen Kameraperspektiven zu rekonstruieren.

industrial:bosch:744000148957129.desc:
Join our innovative research team. We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop a microfluidic sample-preparation unit operation, based on magnetic beads, enabling next-generation molecular diagnostics (MDx) workflows. Next-generation molecular diagnostics require robust and automated methods for isolating low-abundance biological targets - such as pathogens, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), and extracellular vesicles (EVs)-from complex samples. This PhD project aims to develop a scalable, cartridge-compatible platform for the controlled handling of functionalized magnetic particles […] hroughout the complete sample-preparation workflow, including target capture, washing, transfer, resuspension, and release. The central objective is to establish a reusable microfluidic actuation module that interfaces seamlessly with disposable diagnostic cartridges.
 You will conduct targeted literature research on the manipulation of magnetic particles and develop multiphysics models (e.g., COMSOL) to optimize particle trajectories and fluid interactions.
 Furthermore, you will conceptually design and develop a reusable, cartridge-compatible microfluidic handling module that automates the entire target-molecule extraction process (capture, washing, transfer, and release).
 You will create functional prototypes and experimentally quantify system performance using key metrics such as target-molecule recovery, processing time, and reproducibility.
 Last but not least, you will translate your physical understanding and modeling results into rigorous design rules for integration into disposable diagnostics cartridges, delivering transferable models and prototypes for future product development.

 Der Arbeitsbeginn ist im Januar 2027 oder nach Vereinbarung.
 Projekthintergrund
 Während die Weltbevölkerung weiter wächst, verzeichnen viele europäische […] nger einen Bevölkerungsrückgang. Ein Bevölkerungsrückgang wird oft implizit mit negativen Folgen für das gesellschaftliche Wohlergehen in Verbindung gebracht, darunter vermehrter Druck auf das Wirtschaftswachstum, auf die öffentlichen Finanzen, die Arbeitsmärkte und die öffentliche Versorgung. Die Folgen eines Bevölkerungsrückgangs sind jedoch komplex und können auch potenzielle Chancen mit sich bringen. Beispiele dafür sind eine Entlastung der Infrastruktur oder ein verringerter Druck auf Ressourcen und die Umwelt. Die öffentliche Wahrnehmung zu verstehen ist besonders relevant, denn sie beeinflusst nicht nur das individuelle Verhalten, sondern auch den öffentlichen Diskurs und gesellschaftliche Reaktionen.
 Ziel dieser Doktorarbeit ist es, die Wahrnehmung potenzieller Chancen und Risiken im Zusammenhang mit dem Bevölkerungsrückgang zu untersuchen und dazu beizutragen, die Faktoren, welche diese Wahrnehmung beeinflussen, zu identifizieren und zu verstehen.

 The Optical Materials Engineering Laboratory (Prof. David J. Norris) in the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering (D-MAVT) at ETH Zurich investigates the synthesis, growth, structure, and optical properties of nanomaterials. Our interdisciplinary and international team combines materials chemistry, optical spectroscopy, electron microscopy, […] al modeling, and numerical simulation to understand and control materials at the nanoscale.
 Project background
 Nanometer-scale semiconductor crystallites exhibit optical properties (e.g., absorption and emission spectra) that are strongly dependent on their size. Because this property is useful for creating tunable optical materials for optoelectronic applications ranging from displays and infrared cameras to nanophotonics and quantum technologies, chemical syntheses have been developed that produce nanocrystals from various semiconductors. The most advanced protocols are those that lead to quasi-spherical particles (known as colloidal quantum dots). However, even state-of-the-art nanocrystal samples contain distributions in particle size and morphology that limit their optical performance.
 Two classes of semiconductor nanocrystals have been discovered as exceptions to this rule. They display an unusual form of "discrete" growth, jumping between a series of specific sizes. In particular, "magic-sized" nanocrystals grow through a sequence of well-defined sizes. This observation suggests that nanocrystals with exceptionally precise dimensions may be possible.

 En ce début d'année 2025, l'épidémie de grippe saisonnière a une nouvelle fois démontré l'importance de cet agent pathogène en santé humaine. La cause de la maladie est un virus à ARN négatif segmenté dont le génome est constitué de huit molécules trouvées sous forme de ribonucléoprotéine (RNPs) (1). Les segments d'ARN sont uniformément recouverts par la nucléoprotéine (NP), avec leurs extrémités 5' et 3' liées à l'ARN-polymérase hétérotrimérique, formant ainsi des suprastructures moléculaires en double hélice antiparallèle (2). L'équipe a travaillé par le passé sur différents aspects de l'ARN-polymérase (3,4).  L’adaptation des bâtiments aux conditions climatiques estivales constitue un enjeu majeur pour limiter les situations de surchauffe tout en maîtrisant les consommations énergétiques. Dans ce contexte, les enveloppes intégrant des matériaux biosourcés présentent un intérêt particulier en raison de leurs propriétés thermiques et hydriques.
 Le béton de bois constitue une solution constructive biosourcée utilisée notamment pour la réalisation de murs et de systèmes préfabriqués. Ses performances hygrothermiques à l’échelle du système constructif et du bâtiment nécessitent cependant d’être mieux caractérisées, en particulier concernant le confort d’été, l’efficacité énergétique et le comportement face aux situations de surchauffe.

 Description du sujet
 La fabrication des disques de turbine en superalliages passe par différentes opérations de déformation à chaud et de traitement thermique au cours desquelles la microstructure évolue. 
Ces évolutions conditionnent la microstructure finale du matériau, donc la capacité du matériau à soutenir les conditions de température et de contrainte sévères vues
en service, et la durée de vie de la pièce. 
Par ailleurs, afin de repousser encore les températures limites des superalliages employés et leurs performances mécaniques, des nuances de plus en plus alliées sont évaluées.
La complexité croissante de ces alliages appelle, par ricochet, à une remise en question des modèles et des simulations généralement pratiquées dans l'état de l'art pour discuter de l'évolution des joints de grains lors des mécanismes de recristallisation et de croissance de grains en présence de populations complexes de particules de seconde phase, particulièrement pour les superalliages de type γ-γ'.

 Les hétérostructures de van der Waals bidimensionnelles (2D), composées de graphène et de dichalcogénures de métaux de transition, se sont imposées comme une plateforme fascinante pour explorer l'interaction entre de fortes corrélations électroniques et une topologie de bande non triviale, comme l'illustre la récente observation de cristaux de Wigner/Hall et d'isolants de Hall quantiques anormaux fractionnaires au sein de super-réseaux de moiré de graphène rhomboédrique alignés avec du hBN, dont les excitations non abéliennes présentent un intérêt majeur pour le calcul quantique sans décohérence.

 The PhD project 
 Carbon–nitrogen (C–N) bond formation from CO₂ and ammonia or amines is central to carbon capture technologies, atmospheric chemistry, and potentially prebiotic chemistry. A landmark recent study by our experimental partner at ETH Zürich (Signorell group) demonstrated that aqueous microdroplets promote the spontaneous formation of urea from CO₂ and ammonia under ambient conditions, a reaction that does not proceed in bulk solution. This striking microdroplet catalysis reveals reactivity fundamentally different from that of homogeneous solution, yet its molecular origin remains unknown. No predictive framework currently exists to describe or control such chemistry in confined aqueous environments.
 The MICADO project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying microdroplet catalysis of CO₂–amine C–N bond formation and to build the first predictive, multiscale model linking droplet physicochemical properties to reaction rates and product distributions. To achieve this, the ENS team will develop machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained at hybrid-DFT accuracy using active learning protocols, building on the group’s ArcaNN automated training framework and state-of-the-art foundation models such as MACE-OMOL. However, their primary supply is limited and geopolitically constrained, while current recycling processes remain inefficient at recovering these elements from waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE). These metals are typically present at low concentrations in complex matrices and often occur as oxoanionic species, making their selective extraction particularly challenging.

 The PhD project 
 The aim of the project is to enhance the resolution NMR using deep learning. The methods will be developed for the investigation of dynamics in complex ionic liquids with ultrafast high-resolution relaxometry, a method we have recently introduced, allowing us to measure relaxation in the range 100 µT–21 T on a world-unique 900 MHz NMR spectrometer.
 Ionic liquids are materials with unique properties (thermal stability, negligible vapor pressure…) as solvents for environmentally friendly chemistry and efficient energy storage. In particular, solvate ionic liquids (SILs), in which the cation is chelated, are promising candidates to be included as components in a wide range of battery systems. By tailoring the composition of a SIL, its properties can be finely tuned, making SILs promising candidates for safer and more environmentally friendly battery electrolytes.
 As ionic-liquid samples become more complex, particularly in the case of SILs and water-in-solvate ionic liquids (WISILs), their investigation by proton nuclear magnetic resonance becomes more challenging. Proton nuclear magnetic resonance is a powerful method to determine the structure, dynamics and interactions of a variety of molecular systems. …

 The PhD project 
 Achieving carbon neutrality by 2050 requires the rapid deployment of reliable carbon capture, storage and utilization (CCUS) technologies. A major limitation is the lack of experimental data acquired under controlled but industrially relevant conditions, especially for reactive, corrosive and multiphase fluids. This PhD project will develop a robust high-pressure microfluidic platform for the quantitative study and monitoring of CCUS processes. The device will be designed to operate up to 100 bar, between -25 deg C and 80 deg C, with dense or supercritical CO2 and highly corrosive fluids, including concentrated H2SO4 and HNO3 when required. It will be coupled to in situ analytical tools, in particular micro-Raman spectroscopy, optical imaging,pressure/flow/temperature control and machine-learning algorithms for data analysis and autonomous optimization.
 Microfluidics is particularly well suited to this objective because it enables precise control of flow rate, pressure, temperature and composition, while generating large datasets on fast and localized phenomena such as reaction kinetics, mass transfer and precipitation.  Description du sujet
 Our goal in this project is to develop an environmentally responsible upcycling process that can handle both diverse mixed plastic wastes and intractable plastics […]  in today's and tomorrow's landfills. Our methodology is to develop a multi-stage reactor system, with each stage controlled under different experimental conditions. First, we will remove valuable products such as additives and carbon fibers, then convert the remainder into valuable chemicals, including monomers and aromatics. A pyrolytic end-process for treating waste materials from this process will be examined, which can be utilized by refiners. Our goal is to minimize carbon loss through this novel reactor design process, examining both model polymeric systems and real waste streams. We will investigate various downstream refining processes.

 Description du sujet
 Phase transformations (PT) shape the formation of rocks and determine the mechanical properties of many engineered materials, making them a key area of research in both Earth Science and Metallurgy. When subjected to changes in environmental conditions such as pressure or temperature, rocks and metals undergo PTs to achieve thermodynamic equilibrium. In minerals, investigation of mineral assemblages provides essential insights into their conditions of formation. The mineral phases can indeed be used to trace significant geodynamic processes, such as orogenesis, rifting or subduction. In metallic materials, the development of multiple phases is critical for optimizing performance and is an important ingredient in the design of high performance parts in aeronautics, energy, transport, and plenty of other domains. The theory behind the aforementioned PTs relies on the assumption that the stress has the same effect on phase equilibrium as equivalent hydrostatic pressure, meaning the effects of deviatoric stress are neglected. Such hypothesis, however, have recently triggered discussions in both Earth science and Metallurgy.  Description du […] jet
 I. Contexte 
 Au cours de l’obésité, le tissu adipeux (TA) est progressivement infiltré par des cellules immunes pro- inflammatoires dont les macrophages et lymphocytes inflammatoires de type Th1, et Th17, ce qui contribue à l’insulino-résistance et au diabète de type 2.Nous avons rapporté que les cellules souches mésenchymateuses du tissu adipeux (TA) du sujet obèse (ob-CSA) contribuent à l’inflammation et l’insulino-résistance du TA obèse en activant les lymphocytes Th17 pathogéniques, connus pour être impliqués dans bon nombres de maladies inflammatoires chroniques, auto-immunes et/ou cancéreuses 1-3 . 
 II. Objectifs
 Nous souhaitons identifier in vitro , le ou les anticorps capables d’inhiber l’activation des lymphocytes Th17 pathogéniques parmi 15 candidats . Puis nous utiliserons un modèle murin d’obésité, afin d’évaluer dans un modèle physiologique , leur capacité à inhiber la prise de poids, améliorer la tolérance au glucose et la sensibilité à l’insuline, inhiber la stéatose hépatique, la dyslipidémie, l’inflammation du TA, notamment l’infiltration de cellules immunes inflammatoires et la sécrétion de cytokines pro-inflammatoires.
 III. Methodologie:
 Culture cellulaire, tests fonctionnels, Cytometrie en flux, ELISA, RT-PCR, si besoin: tests métaboliques in vivo, Immunofluorescence sur coupes histologiques

 Description du sujet
 Cette thèse s’inscrit dans le projet ANR APPEARANCE_ON_DEMAND (démarrage en 2026), en collaboration entre l’institut iLM (UMR CNRS 5306) et l’institut XLIM (UMR CNRS 7252). L’objectif du projet est de maîtriser la reproduction de l’apparence des matériaux en contrôlant finement leur BRDF (Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function), une fonction qui décrit comment une surface réfléchit la lumière selon les directions d’éclairage et d’observation. La BRDF est étroitement liée à la microtopographie de la surface. Une surface lisse renvoie la lumière différemment d’une surface texturée, mais le lien entre forme microscopique et apparence reste complexe, notamment à cause des réflexions multiples entre les microstructures.
 L’originalité de cette thèse repose sur une approche inverse : au lieu de partir d’une surface donnée pour prédire son apparence, il s’agira de partir d’une BRDF cible, et donc d’un effet visuel voulu, et de déterminer la microtopographie capable de la produire, tout en respectant les contraintes de fabrication (impression en relief via la technologie Mihaly, partenaire industriel du projet ANR).  Description du sujet
 Les matériaux composites, en […] iculier les polymères renforcés de fibres (PRF), sont aujourd’hui largement utilisés pour le renforcement et la réparation des structures en béton armé. Si leur efficacité mécanique est bien établie dans des conditions standards, leur comportement en présence de fissures, notamment pour des ouvertures importantes, reste encore insuffisamment compris. Par ailleurs, leur capacité à assurer une fonction d’étanchéité ainsi que les mécanismes d’endommagement associés soulèvent des enjeux majeurs en termes de durabilité.
 L’objectif de cette thèse est de mener une étude expérimentale approfondie du comportement de composites collés sur support béton fissuré, en s’intéressant aux mécanismes de pontage de fissure, à l’étanchéité du système, ainsi qu’aux processus d’endommagement et de rupture. La thèse s’effectuera dans le cadre du Labcom ANR LCPMC², laboratoire commun entre l’université Lyon 1 (LMC²) et la société SPPM.
 Objectifs scientifiques 
Les objectifs principaux sont les suivants :
 Caractériser expérimentalement le comportement mécanique de systèmes composites collés sur béton fissuré, sous sollicitations monotones et cycliques. 
 Étudier les mécanismes de pontage de fissure , en analysant le transfert d’efforts entre le béton fissuré et le composite.

 Description du sujet
 We are looking for a motivated PhD […] te to work on detection of cyber-malicious actions in distributed power grid systems at INSA Lyon (France). This thesis is co-supervized by LAAS-CNRS.
Future energy networks will increasingly rely on interconnected and distributed infrastructures integrating photovoltaic systems, battery storage, buildings, electric vehicles, and local controllers. While this evolution is essential for the energy transition, it also creates new vulnerabilities to cyber-malicious actions targeting control signals, measurements, and local decision-making units.
The PhD will focus on the detection and classification of intelligent cyberattacks targeting local controllers in distributed power grid systems.
 The main research directions include:
- Modelling distributed power grid systems and their local controllers
- Reviewing fault detection methods, including model-based, observer-based, and machine-learning approaches
- Identifying markers of intelligent, intentional, and malicious manipulations of detection systems
- Developing detection and classification methods to distinguish faults, disturbances, and cyberattacks
- Testing and validating the proposed approaches through simulation and experimental scenarios, with possible validation on the Grid4Mobility platform at INSA Lyon.

 1. Contexte 
 Les […] urs de refroidissement humides, communément appelées systèmes WET, sont largement adoptées dans l’industrie en raison de leur efficacité thermique. Cependant, le prélèvement d’eau directement dans le milieu naturel, nécessaire à leur fonctionnement, soulève aujourd’hui des préoccupations majeures, notamment dans un contexte de stress hydrique croissant et de raréfaction des ressources en eau. 
 Face à cette problématique, il existe une alternative, les tours de refroidissement sèches (DRY), qui se distinguent par une performance supérieure en matière d’économie d’eau. Néanmoins, ces systèmes présentent des limites significatives, tant sur le plan des coûts d’investissement et d’exploitation (CAPEX et OPEX), que sur celui de la performance thermique. 
 Dans un environnement marqué par des contraintes réglementaires de plus en plus strictes et une pression économique accrue, il devient impératif d’optimiser les systèmes WET afin de réduire au maximum les prélèvements et la consommation d’eau, tout en maintenant une performance thermique élevée et en maîtrisant les coûts d’installation et de maintenance.
 Ce projet s’appuie sur le partenariat entre l’entreprise John Cockerill Hamon et le laboratoire CETHIL, reconnu pour son expertise en thermique et énergétique, favorisant une collaboration étroite entre l’industrie et la recherche.

 Le CEA Gramat réalise des expériences de dynamique rapide avec différentes métrologies, qui sont nécessaires à la comparaison expérience/calcul. Pour les calculs, des équations d’état thermodynamique sont utilisées. Pour la comparaison, la spectrométrie et la pyrométrie dynamiques sont développées.
L'institut ICARE-CNRS réalise des mesures de température sur des particules avec des moyens expérimentaux adaptés. L'ensemble de ces moyens optiques requiert un calibrage complexe avant utilisation. Le CEA Gramat et l'Institut ICARE disposent de plusieurs corps noirs complémentaires pour les étalonner. En parallèle de ces moyens de mesure ponctuels, les développements récents des caméras rapides permettent de les utiliser d'une façon similaire à un pyromètre sur une surface ou un volume, à l'aide d'un montage optique spécifique.
Les objectifs de la thèse sont d'appliquer la spectrométrie dynamique pour la mesure du flux thermique et la vidéo numérique rapide à un milieu semi-transparent pour étudier les différentes phases d'initiation, combustion, déflagration sous pression de particules et/ou matériaux énergétiques .

 Main objective of the thesis: 
 The main objective of the PhD is to develop a distributed, federated framework for predictive and prescriptive management of multi-energy systems, enabling coordination among multiple actors while preserving the privacy and confidentiality of their data. The research will combine predictive models, for instance, for forecasting energy demand, renewable generation, available flexibility, or future system states, with prescriptive methods determining appropriate actions for generation, storage and flexible consumption.
 Particular emphasis will be placed on Federated Learning (FL), enabling multiple actors to collaboratively train models without centralising their operational data. The research will investigate how FL can go beyond conventional forecasting applications and become part of an integrated decision-making framework linking prediction with the coordinated operation of distributed energy resources. Coordination among actors will be addressed through a multi-agent architecture and distributed coordination mechanisms, including approaches based on game theory and distributed optimisation.  The main objective of the thesis is to develop a trustworthy AI framework for the predictive control of multi-energy systems ensuring a safe operation in real-time, considering interactions between different energy vectors, renewable generation, storage and energy conversion technologies.
 The developed approaches will aim to exploit the flexibility available across the different energy infrastructures while respecting their physical and operational constraints. Particular attention will be paid to the ability of the proposed methods to operate under uncertainty and disturbances and to provide control decisions within computational times compatible with real-time operation.  Intitulé du sujet

Nevertheless, the physical phenomena governing LFW remain particularly complex. Heat is generated through friction and severe plastic deformation, while the resulting temperature increase strongly affects the material behaviour, contact conditions, interfacial friction, material flow, and bonding mechanisms. These phenomena are highly coupled and evolve rapidly during the different stages of the process. Moreover, the final weld quality depends not only on macroscopic variables, such as temperature, stress, strain, flash formation, and applied force, but also on microstructural transformations occurring at and around the interface. An inadequate combination of operating parameters may therefore lead to insufficient bonding, voids, cracks, or undesirable microstructural changes.
Experimental investigations provide essential information for understanding these mechanisms. However, the high cost of testing, the short duration of the process, and the difficulty of accessing the welding interface during operation limit the amount of information that can be obtained experimentally. Furthermore, extensive experimental campaigns are generally required for each new material and welding configuration. High-fidelity numerical models can complement these investigations by predicting the thermomechanical history, material flow, contact behaviour, and microstructure evolution. …

 Cette thèse vise à modéliser avec précision l’intonation des instruments à anches doubles (binious et bombardes) afin de reconstituer les tempéraments musicaux utilisés en Bretagne au début du XXe siècle. La démarche s’appuie sur des mesures et modèles physiques réalisées sur des instruments d’époque.
 Dans un premier temps, une caractérisation expérimentale des instruments, des résonateurs et des anches sera menée, que ce soit en contexte quasi-statique (sans auto-oscillations) ou à l’aide d’un musicien artificiel à développer (auto-oscillations). Les données recueillies serviront à enrichir des modèles physiques existants, qui devront être adaptés spécifiquement aux binious et bombardes.
 Les résultats obtenus pourront ensuite être mis en relation avec l’étude de l’intonation menée dans le cadre d’un autre volet du projet ANR.

En dynamique rapide, les conditions sont quasi adiabatiques et le matériau subit un auto-échauffement plastique à l’origine d’un adoucissement ou/et de transformations microstructurales. La bonne prise en compte des couplages thermomécaniques dans la modélisation constitutive nécessite donc des mesures couplées cinématiques et thermiques lors de la caractérisation.
Le projet de thèse a pour objectif de développer un jumeau numérique des dispositifs d’essai rapide de compression et de traction par barres d’Hopkinson, s’appuyant sur la corrélation d’images numériques cinématiques et thermiques, rendant compte des incertitudes métrologiques et numériques, et visant la calibration de modèles de comportement thermo-viscoplastiques.
L’approche sera d’abord appliquée à un acier doux (S355) puis étendue à d’autres matériaux. Le moyen expérimental principal sera constitué des dispositifs d’essai rapide de compression et de traction par barres d’Hopkinson, acquis récemment par le CEA …

 Description du sujet
 La détonation d'un explosif crée une onde de choc qui se propage dans l'air et le met en mouvement de façon brutale. Ce phénomène, appelé effet de souffle, est à l'origine des dégâts induits par l'explosion. Le souffle peut être renforcé par des réactions de combustion : celle des produits de détonation avec l'air et celle de particules métalliques incluses dans la charge spécifiquement dans ce but.
La modélisation macroscopique du souffle est actuellement traitée avec un modèle empirique. L’augmentation de son périmètre d’utilisation nécessite d’introduire de la physique identifiée à l’échelle mésoscopique grâce à des simulations LES (Large Eddy Simulations) multiphasiques et réactives. De précédents travaux ont permis d'aboutir à une méthodologie numérique permettant de simuler de façon efficace et robuste l'écoulement réactif au sein des boules de feu. Il s'agit désormais de l'exploiter pour développer un nouveau modèle macroscopique de postcombustion.

 Description du sujet
 Le CEA Gramat est le centre expert des effets des armes, notamment les armes électromagnétiques. Il réalise à ce titre des études de vulnérabilité et de susceptibilité de systèmes soumis à des agressions électromagnétiques (EM) diverses. Depuis plusieurs décennies la miniaturisation et l’intégration de l’électronique a permis de faire émerger des systèmes de radiocommunication très compacts et complexes mais également potentiellement plus vulnérables vis-à-vis d’une agression EM intentionnelle.
L’amplificateur faible bruit (LNA) constitue généralement le premier composant actif de l’étage d’entrée d’une chaîne de réception RF. C’est pourquoi il constitue l’élément dimensionnant face à une telle agression. Afin de limiter cette menace ou de s’en affranchir, une bonne connaissance des effets des agressions EM sur un LNA est essentielle et il s'agit d'identifier de potentielles architectures qui présenteraient une robustesse à ces effets.
L’objectif de la thèse est de proposer une nouvelle architecture de LNA capable de supporter différents types d'agressions EM impulsionnelles.

 Le constat alarmant de la perte de 65 000 hectares de terres chaque année en France lié à l’urbanisation, l'équivalent d'un département tous les 10 ans, ne peut être ignoré. Cette expansion urbaine accentue considérablement les conséquences du ruissellement pluvial et contribue à la dégradation de la qualité des eaux urbaines. En favorisant l’imperméabilisation des sols, l’urbanisation amplifie les volumes ruisselés, tandis que l’intensification des évènements climatiques (inondations, fortes chaleurs, sècheresse…) rend les territoires plus vulnérables. Dans ce contexte, le développement des stratégies d’adaptation des territoires devient essentiel pour préserver la ressource en eau. Les chaussées imperméables, dont les seules voiries communales représentent 46 200 km pour la Région Grand Est, offrent à ce titre un fort potentiel de désimperméabilisation.  Description du sujet
 Avec le riz et le maïs, le blé fait partie des trois principales espèces végétales cultivées dans le monde et notamment en France, avec plus de cinq millions d’hectares dédiés à cette culture. Cette culture est soumise à une forte pression parasitaire. Les principales maladies qui touchent le blé sont la septoriose, la fusariose de l’épis et les rouilles, responsables en moyenne à 15 à 20% de perte de rendement par an (Figueroa et al., 2018). L’inoculum primaire est la source initiale de pathogène qui combiné aux facteurs climatiques est responsable l’épidémie dans les parcelles. Cet inoculum est essentiellement inféodé à la parcelle pour la septoriose et la fusariose de l’épis ou provient d’échelle plus large (rouilles). Pour la fusariose de l’épis, causée par un complexe d’agents pathogène dont Fusarium graminearum , l’incidence de l’épidémie est fortement corrélée aux conditions météorologiques ainsi qu’à l’abondance de l’inoculum primaire (i.e source initiale de contamination responsable de l’épidémie) (Alisaac et al., 2023). 
 Il est donc important de caractériser les facteurs qui influencent la présence de cet inoculum primaire (en quantité et virulence) et sa répartition …

 Übersicht 
 Doctoral position in theoretical modeling of nanocrystal growth
 100%, Zurich, fixed-term 
 print 
 Drucken 
 The Optical Materials Engineering Laboratory (Prof. David J. Norris) in the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering (D-MAVT) at ETH Zurich investigates the synthesis, growth, structure, and optical properties of semiconductor nanomaterials. Our interdisciplinary and international team combines materials chemistry, optical spectroscopy, electron microscopy, theoretical modeling, and […] erical simulation to understand and control materials at the nanoscale.
 Project background
 Nanometer-scale semiconductor crystallites exhibit optical properties (e.g., absorption and emission spectra) that are strongly dependent on their size. Because this property is useful for creating tunable optical materials for optoelectronic applications ranging from displays and infrared cameras to nanophotonics and quantum technologies, chemical syntheses have been developed that produce nanocrystals from various semiconductors. The most advanced protocols are those that lead to quasi-spherical particles (known as colloidal quantum dots). However, even state-of-the-art nanocrystal samples contain distributions in particle size and morphology that limit their optical performance.
 Two classes of semiconductor nanocrystals have been discovered as exceptions to this rule. They display an unusual form of "discrete" growth, jumping between a series of specific sizes. Semiconductor nanoplatelets can be synthesized with atomically uniform thicknesses, while so-called "magic-sized" nanocrystals grow through a sequence of well-defined sizes. These observations suggest that nanocrystals with exceptionally precise dimensions may be possible. Nevertheless, the mechanisms that govern whether nanoplatelets, magic-sized nanocrystals, or conventional colloidal quantum dots form from a specific …

 Mots clés 
 biophysics, cell biology, mathematical […] ng 
 Description du sujet
 Cell volume is fundamental to biological organisation, controlling molecular concentration, intracellular transport, membrane tension and cytoplasmic mechanics. Cell volume emerges from coupled osmotic and hydrostatic pressures, water movement across the membrane, intracellular poroelasticity and active ion regulation operating from milliseconds to minutes. These overlapping processes are difficult to distinguish using conventional imaging.
 This interdisciplinary PhD will combine ultrafast quantitative phase imaging, microfluidic pressure control and mechanistic modelling to identify the physical parameters that govern cell-volume regulation. The project builds directly on our previous BBSRC Transformative Research Technologies award, which developed advanced QPI and open tools for mechanobiology. Operating above 300 frames per second, our label-free platform can measure the earliest volume responses before slower active regulation dominates.
 The student will apply precisely controlled osmotic and hydrostatic pressure stimuli, including steps, pulses, ramps and oscillations, to living cells. These perturbations will provide a form of “pressure–volume spectroscopy”, enabling the candidate to quantify the dynamics of cellular water transport: how rapidly water crosses the plasma membrane, redistributes within the cytoplasm, and is subsequently …

Contexte scientifique USTS développe un projet d’IA souveraine, entièrement exécuté sur une infrastructure locale, pour permettre aux entreprises de garder le contrôle de leurs données et de leurs systèmes, tout en préservant la précision et la qualité des résultats. La thèse s’intéresse aux systèmes fondés sur des modèles de […]  capables d’accomplir des tâches séquentielles : exploiter des informations, interagir avec des outils, conserver des connaissances et adapter leurs actions aux résultats obtenus. Dans ce cadre, la réussite dépend de décisions prises à différents moments de l’exécution, dont les conséquences peuvent être différées. Le choix d’une information à conserver influence les actions futures. Le choix d’un modèle détermine le coût et la qualité d’une étape. Une vérification peut éviter la propagation d’une erreur, mais consomme des ressources supplémentaires. La mémoire, les actions et l’utilisation des modèles constituent ainsi des composantes interdépendantes du processus de décision. Le problème étudié sera celui de l’apprentissage de stratégies coordonnées pour ces composantes, dans un environnement où les informations évoluent et où le calcul disponible est limité. Question scientifique et hypothèses Comment apprendre conjointement des stratégies de mémoire, d’action et d’utilisation des modèles qui maintiennent la fiabilité des tâches séquentielles lorsque les informations évoluent et que les ressources de calcul sont limitées ? Une hypothèse centrale est que l’apprentissage de ces stratégies à partir de la réussite des tâches complètes peut améliorer le compromis entre fiabilité et coût de calcul par rapport à des stratégies optimisées séparément. uzh-phd:10220199.title: Three PhD Positions in Computational Astrophysics
uzh-phd:10220199.desc:
The research covers three broad, overlapping areas:
 Flagship simulations: Develop and run the next-generation Euclid Flagship simulation with PKDGRAV3 on GPU-accelerated supercomputers. This includes extending the code to identify dark matter halos and their substructure on the fly, and working with our partners to turn the simulation into mock galaxy catalogues for Euclid.
 Emulators: Build the next generation of the Euclid Emulator: machine-learning models, trained on large suites of simulations, that predict cosmological statistics in milliseconds. The goal is to extend the emulator from the matter distribution to galaxy clustering and lensing statistics.
 Baryonification and multi-probe cosmology: Model how gas and stars alter the matter distribution predicted by N-body simulations, and develop a pipeline that produces consistent synthetic sky maps (weak lensing, galaxy clustering, X-ray and Sunyaev–Zel'dovich) for Euclid and complementary surveys.
This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of astrophysics and advanced computational methods. Applicants are expected to hold a master's degree (or equivalent) in physics, astronomy or a related field by the starting date.
Candidates with a strong interest in high-performance computing, machine learning or numerical astrophysics are especially encouraged to apply. Programming experience is an asset. from 1 January 2027

at-nl:364762.desc:
The Faculty of Science and Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for candidates for a PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN
ANA-KIN is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme. Over the past two decades, small-molecule kinase inhibitors have transformed cancer therapy, yet nearly all of them target the highly conserved ATP-binding site, which limits selectivity and allows resistance to emerge. ANA-KIN aims to train a new generation of […] skills.
In this PhD project (DC10, Work Package 3 – Discovery), you will develop deep-learning architectures that integrate text-mined, cheminformatic, and biophysical descriptors to predict interface binding, allosteric signatures and resistance liabilities of kinase ligands. The models will learn jointly across peptide and small-molecule modalities and will be used to generate hybrid peptidomimetic design hypotheses. You will translate these models into consortium-wide prioritisation dashboards that support hit triage and analogue selection in the discovery campaigns of ANA-KIN, and work in close reciprocal feedback with DC9 (Saarland University) on structure-based and machine-learning pipelines. Model predictions will be validated prospectively with the experimental partners in the network.
The expected results are a resistance-aware AI workflow for non-ATP interface ligands, accompanied by public models, datasets and interpretable feature maps, and prospective design case studies demonstrating improved optimisation trajectories. To reinforce structural grounding and experimental validation, you will carry out two secondments: at VIB (Belgium, Prof. Ruslan Efremov; 4 months) to extract structural classes and conformational features from cryo-EM data and use them to refine model constraints, and at Skylight Therapeutics (Belgium, Dr. Joshua Salafsky; 3 months) to test model …

 Description du sujet
 Les surfaces antiadhésives utilisées dans le secteur de la boulangerie, viennoiserie et pâtisserie reposente encore largement sur des revêtements contenant des substances per- et polyfluoroalkylées (PFAS), notamment le PTFE. L’évolution rapide du contexte réglementaire et les préoccupations environnementales et sanitaires associées aux PFAS rendent nécessaire le développement de solutions alternatives performantes, durables et compatibles avec le contact alimentaire.
 Le projet ANR SAFE-BAKE vise à mieux comprendre les phénomènes intervenant à l’interface entre les surfaces de cuisson et les produits alimentaires et à développer des solutions PFAS-free. Il considère à la fois des solutions directement accessibles à l’industrie, reposant notamment sur l’utilisation de surfaces métalliques associées à des agents de démoulage, et des approches à plus long terme fondées sur l’ingénierie de surface.
 L’un des enjeux est de comprendre les relations entre la topographie, la physicochimie et les propriétés interfaciales des surfaces, leur évolution au cours de l’utilisation et leurs performances antiadhésives.

The BRIDGE-AI doctoral network is employing 15 ambitious doctoral candidates at various locations in Europe (Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Switzerland and Austria). We are currently inviting applications for the last 3 open PhD positions, located in Germany and Finland (see below). The aim of the BRIDGE-AI network is to develop new and trustworthy AI methods for longitudinal neuroimage analysis, helping clinical experts assess temporal changes in patients with chronic brain disorders. More information about the project is available from the BRIDGE-AI website .
DC1: Deep learning for cortical surface-based analyses (Bonn, Germany)
Employer: German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE)
Main supervisor: Prof. Dr. Martin Reuter

Are you passionate about advancing neuroscience and clinical applications through cutting-edge AI technology? Do you want to contribute to tools that can transform how we understand brain function, study neurological diseases, and evaluate large-scale population studies? Join us to develop innovative AI methods for cortical surface modeling – an essential foundation for modern neuroimaging research.

Why This Matters: The cerebral cortex, with its intricate folds and complex structure, holds key insights into brain health and disease. Accurate modeling and analysis of the cortical surface enable breakthroughs in understanding brain development, detecting abnormalities, and tracking disease progression. Your work will help build powerful AI tools that can improve diagnosis, guide treatment strategies, and push the boundaries of neuroscience research.
In this PhD project, you will:
Develop advanced AI methods to segment brain cortical atlases based on surface data, moving beyond traditional approaches.
Create algorithms to detect anomalies on the cortical surface, such as Focal Cortical Dysplasia (FCD), aiding early diagnosis of neurological conditions.
Innovate deep learning solutions for longitudinal surface extraction, tracking brain changes over time with unprecedented accuracy.
Implement state-of-the-art deep learning techniques for cross-subject and cross-time surface registration.
Thoroughly validate your methods to ensure broad applicability in neuroimaging workflows.

Your contributions will elevate the accuracy, reliability, and generalizability of cortical surface analysis, setting new standards for the field. They will generate impact through their possible integration into widely used neuroimaging pipelines such as FastSurfer and FreeSurfer.

What We Offer: We are the developers of FastSurfer and co-developers of FreeSurfer , world-leading open-source neuroimage analysis pipelines. We are experts in developing advanced deep-learning methods for medical image processing. At our lab you will have access to excellent supervision and to a powerful computational environment, including a high-performance cluster with close to one hundred NVIDIA 32GB GPUs and four dedicated servers reserved exclusively for our group, each with 8 GPUs (32-40GB RAM each). Furthermore, we offer research stays at world-renowned institutions, including the Martinos Center at MGH and Harvard Medical School, Boston USA, as well as Icometrix, Belgium. We provide a dynamic, collaborative research environment with mentorship from experts in AI, neuroimaging, and clinical neuroscience.
You hold a strong background in computer science, biomedical engineering, applied mathematics, or a related field.
You have experience in machine learning and deep learning with applications in medical imaging or neuroscience.
You are motivated to work on impactful research that bridges AI development with real-world neurological applications.
You possess solid programming skills (Python and PyTorch) and optimally have worked with geometric representations, such as triangle meshes.
Experience with brain MRI data, or longitudinal analysis is a plus but not mandatory.
If you’re eager to push the frontiers of AI in neuroscience and contribute to transformative research with world-class collaborators and resources, we want to hear from you !

DC9: Interpretable prediction of gestational age from fetal brain MRI across institutions (Espoo, Finland)
PhD enrollment: Aalto University , Espoo, Finland
Main supervisor: prof. Koen Van Leemput

PhD project description: The assessment of whether a fetus is at the expected development stage is currently performed in a rather primitive fashion in the clinic: clinicians manually perform 2D measurements from fetal brain MRI scans, and compare those to normative growth curves to see whether development is delayed. In this PhD project, you will significantly advance this state of affairs by developing new probabilistic generative models of the developing neuroanatomy across gestational ages, and use those models to accurately estimate the gestational age from fetal MRI scans.

This is a highly relevant but also very ambitious project: In order to be fully clinically useful, the methods and tools that you will develop should work “out-of-the-box” on data that is acquired with different scanners, image resolutions, reconstruction algorithms and acquisition protocols. Furthermore, your models should encode the cause-effect relationship between gestational age and the acquired MRI scans, so that the obtained predictions are inherently interpretable for clinicians (for instance, by generating counterfactuals simulating a particular fetus’s neuroanatomy at different gestational ages). Once you are confident in the performance of your methods and tools, you should also apply them to large clinical datasets of both normal and abnormal brain development.

Your profile: This position requires strong skills in both math (e.g., linear algebra, Bayesian statistics) and coding (e.g., Python/NumPy, C++). Prior experience with medical imaging is not required.

prof. Meritxell Bach Cuadra (9 months) at the University of Lausanne (Lausanne, Switzerland)
Dr. Tom Hilbert (2 months) at Siemens Healthineers (Lausanne, Switzerland)
DC14: Longitudinal progression markers derived from WM and GM alterations in different epilepsy phenotypes (Espoo, Finland)
PhD enrollment: Aalto University , Espoo, Finland
Main supervisors: prof. Koen Van Leemput & Dr. Richard McKinley (Bern, Switzerland)

Clinical Problem : Among patients who present with a first seizure, approximately 45% will have a further seizure within the next five years. Identifying which patients are likely to have recurrent seizures is therefore vitally important, since early treatment can dramatically improve the lives of patients with epilepsy and spare them from further neurological deficits brought on by repeated seizures.

Structural brain lesions are the most common cause of epileptic seizures, but the mere presence of a lesion is not predictive of epilepsy: the size and location of the lesion, and its proximity to the grey matter, are critical factors. Similarly, while loss of grey matter is seen in all epilepsy patients over time, specific patterns of grey-matter atrophy can be associated to different epilepsy subtypes. Identifying these patterns in a timely manner has the potential to drive patient treatment.

Your solution : In this PhD project you will develop methods to link patterns of grey- and white-matter alterations to epilepsy subtypes and to distinguish epilepsy patients from those with epilepsy mimics. You will benchmark and extend existing segmentation methods for quantifying white matter lesions and grey matter atrophy, and establish baselines for linking alterations and disease, such as lesion-symptom mapping and structural covariance networks. You will then explore how generative modeling can be harnessed to translate patterns of brain alteration into low-dimensional latent codes which capture the essence of a patient’s deviation from normal brain appearance, and harness these codes to better estimate a patient’s risk of receiving a definitive epilepsy diagnosis. The methods developed will be based on data from, and have direct application in, ongoing studies at the University Hospital Bern and across Switzerland, which aim to identify patients at high risk of developing epilepsy after a first seizure, and to study the effects of epilepsy over time on the structure, function and metabolism of the brain.
Foreseen secondments: For this PhD project, research visits are foreseen to:
Prof Roland Wiest & Dr. Richard McKinley, Inselspital, University Hospital Bern, Switzerland (10 months across 3 visits)
Dr Ankur Sharma, Bayer (Berlin, Germany) (2 months)

CAVECORE Continuous, Automated Validation, and Evaluation of Cognitive Robots in Open-Ended Environments (CAVECORE). "> Funded by The European Union under The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Networks programme Grant Agreement No. 101227310.

CAVECORE (Continuous, Automated Validation, and Evaluation of Cognitive Robots in Open-Ended Environments) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network that trains the next generation of researchers to advance cognitive robotics —robots that can interact, learn, and adapt to open-ended real-world environments. The network addresses one of the central challenges in AI-enabled robotics: evaluating and validating the quality , safety , and reliability of such robots in a systematic and trustworthy manner.

Doctoral Candidates in CAVECORE will follow an interdisciplinary training program that combines expertise in robotics and AI (e.g., learning-enabled manipulation, control, and human-robot interaction) with cutting-edge validation and evaluation methods (e.g., automated testing, diagnosis, analysis, and AI metrology). They will develop novel approaches that make evaluability-by-design a core part of the robot development process, ensuring that cognitive robots provide continuous evidence of their performance and can adapt to evolving societal, ethical, and legal requirements such as those set out in the EU AI Act. By engaging in secondments across leading academic and industrial partners , DCs gain hands-on experience, professional skills, and unique career perspectives. They will be prepared to lead innovation in robotics that is not only technically advanced but also economically viable and socially responsible, with applications ranging from agile production to logistics and maritime robotics.

This Doctoral Network will provide its Doctoral Candidates with a rigorous training in solving complex problems characterised by many degrees of freedom and intrinsic noise, all of which arise in the context of biological systems and are key to functions as movement, growth and regulation. Each Doctoral Candidate will pursue research within one of the PhD Research Projects described below, utilising techniques from statistical and condensed matter physics to discover how collective phenomena emerge in biological systems from interactions between their component parts.

A distinctive feature of this Doctoral Network is that a novel combination of modelling and analysis techniques, which traditionally have each been applied in a specific problem domain, lies at the heart of each PhD research project. For this reason, Doctoral Candidates will each have two supervisors, one at the primary host institution (indicated in the panels below), and another at a second institution in the network, with a period of research at the second institution, fully funded by the programme, designed into the research projects. Some projects additionally feature secondments with our non-academic partners.

Decoding and designing biomolecular systems with hybrid DNA:RNA:protein nanotechnology

Our increasing knowledge of the fundamental mechanisms of life and the confluence of techniques are the basis for the development of novel life-inspired technologies. In recent years, notably in the development of COVID-19 vaccines, we have witnessed the pivotal role played by RNA in nanomedical advancements. At the same time, DNA nanotechnology has already proven to yield some of the most complex, yet well controlled, artificial biomolecular structures.

Taking these different ingredients together, our abilities of building bottom-up functional machines and biomolecular systems involving DNA, RNA and proteins are currently emerging quicker than ever before, with new prospects for drug design and delivery, biosensors, as well as complex biomolecular robots and materials.

To unlock the full potential for complex biosensing devices that modularly emulate life-like functions and interact in complex biomolecular environments, BioHYBRITE brings together a unique team of world leading academics in the forefront of relevant bottom-up hybrid nanotechnologies, through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA DN funding scheme (Grant Agreement Nr. 101227379).

Which positions are open, and when should I apply? Check the vacancy listings and individual doctoral project pages for open positions. Each university advertisement specifies its own application window, requirements and deadline.

How do I submit an application? Read the doctoral project page, then follow its link to the recruiting university’s official advertisement. Submit your application through the procedure specified there. Vacancies will also be advertised on EURAXESS. The EMANAIRE website provides information and links; it does not receive applications.

Can I apply to more than one project? Yes. You may apply to up to four EMANAIRE doctoral projects. Submit a separate application for each position. In each motivation or cover letter, briefly identify your other EMANAIRE applications, including any you intend to submit, using the project numbers or titles. Tailor each application to the project concerned.

What academic background do I need? We welcome applicants interested in the human and organisational implications of AI. Relevant backgrounds may include management, organisation studies, psychology, sociology, communication and information systems. Each project has its own academic, methodological and language requirements, and you must meet the host university’s doctoral admission requirements.

Can I apply if I am still completing my master’s degree? This depends on the university. Check its advertisement for when your qualifying degree must be completed and what evidence you should provide. Contact the recruiting university if you are unsure whether your expected graduation date meets its requirements.

Can applicants of any nationality apply? Yes. MSCA Doctoral Network positions are open to applicants of any nationality. You must also satisfy the mobility rule, doctoral-status condition and the recruiting university’s admission and employment requirements. Visa or residence-permit arrangements depend on your circumstances and the host country.

What is the MSCA mobility rule? In general, you must not have lived or carried out your main activity, such as work or study, in the recruiting country for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment. This is assessed separately for each recruiting country. The university will check your circumstances and any applicable exceptions; consult its advertisement for the full conditions.

Can I apply if I already have a doctorate? You must not hold a doctoral degree when recruited. Researchers who have successfully defended a doctoral thesis are also ineligible, even if the degree has not yet been formally awarded.

Which documents should I prepare? Follow the individual university advertisement. Requirements may include a CV, motivation letter, degree certificates and transcripts, references, a research proposal and evidence of MSCA eligibility. Proposal lengths and document formats differ between hosts. Use the official instructions for each application rather than one standard document package.

Are the positions funded, and how long do they last? The doctoral positions are supported through EMANAIRE’s MSCA funding. Salary, allowances, contract duration and any additional institutional funding are specified by each recruiting university. Check each advertisement for its own employment terms.

Where will I be based, and will I travel? You will be based at the host university listed for your project and join shared network activities. Planned secondments and academic visits provide experience in other research and professional settings. The arrangements for your position, including travel and timing, will be explained by the host university.
When would the doctorate start? Start dates may differ between universities. Follow the intended start date and any flexibility stated in each official university advertisement.

Who can answer questions or help with application adjustments? Use the contact named in the relevant university advertisement for project questions, eligibility checks or reasonable adjustments to the application and selection process. For general questions about the network, contact the EMANAIRE coordinator.

You will develop your project at a host university while joining an international community of doctoral researchers and supervisors. Shared schools, methods workshops and research seminars will support your work, with planned secondments connecting your research to organisations outside academia. Employment terms and application requirements are set out in each official advertisement.

The aim of this project is to simultaneously improve the activity and stability of cytochrome P450 BM3, minimizing trade-off effects and enabling a smoother transition to larger-scale application. To enable this, Lisa will develop a workflow applying high-throughput screening to generate experimental data on the enzyme's sequence and functional properties, which will be used to iteratively train a predictive machine learning model.
Background fields: s tructural biology, molecular biology

Project title: Engineering conformational dynamics and mechanism in oxygenases

The project focuses on the computationally guided design of oxygenases through the engineering of enzyme conformational dynamics and catalytic mechanism. The project aims to understand how changes in protein sequence, including mutations at residues distant from the active site can reshape the conformational ensamble of oxygenases and thereby improve activity and selectivity. In particular, Shortest Path Map (SPM) analyses are used to investigate communication networks within the enzyme and identify pathways connecting distal residues to the active site.
Background fields: b ioinformatics, machine-learning, drug discovery workflows, cheminformatics

Project title: Kinetic stability data collection for predictive bioprocess modelling of CYP enzymes

The main objectives of this project are to understand how dissolved oxygen affects enzyme stability in a bioprocess-realistic environment, as well as to develop a hybrid model to predict enzyme stability across different reactors and conditions. The project will involve a scale-down approach, with a focus on gathering relevant stability data for P450. The collected data will then be used for the development of a hybrid model utilizing active learning and machine learning. The initial work will focus on isolated enzymes, with the ambition of expanding the model to whole-cell systems.
Background fields: m olecular biotechnology, fermentation, biocatalysis
Project title : Process intensification of cytochrome P450 reactions in batch and continuous reactors

This project focuses on intensifying cytochrome P450-catalysed reactions in batch and continuous-flow reactors. Controlled bioreactor experiments and reaction engineering will be used to investigate how substrate supply, and the delivery of oxygen or hydrogen peroxide influence reaction efficiency and productivity. In collaboration with WP1, engineered P450 variants will be evaluated under process-relevant conditions, while the resulting kinetic and process data will contribute to modelling and machine-learning activities in WP3. Selected reactions will also be investigated in pressurized continuous-flow systems to improve oxygen availability. By identifying key process bottlenecks and developing scale-up criteria, the project aims to connect enzyme engineering with robust and scalable biocatalytic production.
Background fields : biotechnology, biochemistry, biocatalysis, bioprocess engineering, continuous-flow biocatalysis
Project title: Process development and optimization of dioxygenase catalysed biotransformation

The project is process development and optimisation of dioxygenase-catalysed biotransformation based on the conversion of isoeugenol to vanillin, focusing on biocatalyst operational stability under bioreactor conditions. The research will combine experimental biocatalyst development, kinetic characterization, mathematical modelling, and in silico process intensification and validation.
Background fields: e nzyme bioprocess, reaction engineering, process intensification, machine learning
Project title: Continuous flow oxyfunctionalisations of allylic substrates catalysed by UPOs

The aim of this project is to develop efficient and reusable unspecific peroxygenase (UPO) biocatalysts for selective oxyfunctionalization. Nektaria will combine protein engineering and process engineering to improve UPO activity, selectivity, stability, and reusability for allylic oxyfunctionalization. Diverse UPOs and allylic substrates will be screened to identify promising enzyme–substrate combinations, while enzyme immobilization, continuous-flow operation, and controlled H₂O₂ supply will be explored to enhance overall catalytic and process performance, enabling more efficient and sustainable oxyfunctionalization chemistry.
Background fields: biotechnology, biochemistry, biocatalysis, protein engineering, and bioprocess engineering
Project title: Machine learning-based tools for multiparametric enzyme optimisation

Daniela's project focuses on developing machine learning-based tools for multiparametric enzyme optimisation. Building on protein mutational datasets generated in-house for a range of enzymes, as well as public protein databases, she will explore and compare state-of-the-art data representation techniques to build next-generation data-driven models for engineering properties such as enzyme activity, selectivity, stability and solubility.
Background fields: computational chemistry, bioinformatics, molecular dynamics
Project title: Development of machine learned coarse grained force fields for computational enzyme design

Filippo works on machine-learned force-fields for enzyme systems — neural network models that learn from reference data the potential energy surface governing how these proteins move. He is particularly interested in coarse-grained models, which enable the simulation of long-timescale dynamics. He is also interested in explainability and interpretability methods, which make machine-learning models transparent rather than black boxes: understanding what the network has learned about the underlying physics and why it produces a given prediction, both to trust the simulations and to extract mechanistic insight into how enzymes work.
Project title: Development of ML-based tools for analysis and engineering protein dynamics

Tillman’s project focuses on developing machine-learning tools to analyse and engineer protein dynamics. These movements and conformational changes play a central role in how enzymes function. The project aims to move beyond static protein structures by developing efficient methods to predict, understand, and deliberately modify dynamic behaviour. He will also develop AI-assisted workflows that support the progression from researching a target protein and computationally screening designs to prioritizing candidates for experimental validation. The broader goal is to establish protein dynamics as a practical component of protein design, enabling useful enzyme variants to be identified with fewer experiments and less computation.
Background fields: machine learning, bioinformatics, scientific software engineering, agentic workflows
Project title: EVB- and AI-guided Engineering of Unspecific Peroxygenases (UPOs) for Selective Benzylic Hydroxylation

Biya's project combines computational methods and machine learning to engineer unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) for selective benzylic C–H hydroxylation, a reaction that competes with off-target epoxidation and overoxidation. Towards this, she will build calibrated EVB/QM/MM models of the enzyme's reaction mechanism to understand how its structure governs this selectivity, and use these insights to propose targeted mutations. The collected simulation data will then be used to develop an uncertainty-aware active learning model that prioritises the enzyme variants most worth testing, rather than screening them all. The project also extends into process engineering, modelling how the enzyme performs under real operating conditions to support its future use at an industrial scale. This combination of mechanistic simulation and data-driven prediction is intended to identify UPO variants and operating conditions that improve selectivity and productivity, with fewer experiments than conventional screening would require.
Background fields: theoretical and computational chemistry, molecular dynamics simulation
Project title: Hybrid models for data-driven bioprocess optimization

Athina's project focuses on developing novel machine learning methods for the design and optimization of bioprocesses in biocatalysis. The objective is to develop an algorithmic toolbox for bioprocess optimization, scale-down process development, control and transfer learning across different processes. The optimization aims to maximize process outcome and minimize experimental resources. Regarding scale-up and scale-down, variable mismatches arise between scales, leading to different effects on the process. For control, the goal is to achieve real-time control under uncertainty, accounting for the nonlinear and dynamic nature of the system. The model will be applied to UPO, CYP and DO production processes, using hybrid models as the modeling method.
Background fields: bioprocess engineering, hybrid modeling, machine learning

The combination of a long coastline, shallow water, and offshore wind makes the UK one of the best locations in the world for wind power. MLCARE – Machine Learning Computational Advancements for peRsonalized mEdicine (HORIZON – MSCA – 2024 – DN – 101226456 – MLCARE)
Machine Learning Computational Advancements for peRsonalized mEdicine (HORIZON – MSCA – 2024 – DN – 101226456 – MLCARE)

Precision medicine represents a paradigm shift in healthcare, transitioning from generalized treatment strategies to highly personalized care. This transformation is driven by rapid advancements in digital technologies, which generate massive volumes of data from diverse sources, including genomic sequences , high-resolution imaging, wearable devices, and electronic health records (EHRs). However, despite an annual estimate of 50 petabytes of data generated per hospital , only a fraction is utilized effectively. Harnessing this untapped potential offers a transformative opportunity to uncover novel disease mechanisms and deliver more precise and effective therapeutic interventions.

The MLCare project seeks to revolutionize precision medicine by developing cutting-edge AI solutions that integrate genomic, clinical, and environmental data into holistic, multimodal patient representations. Through innovative approaches such as Foundation Models and advanced generative AI methods, MLCare will address critical challenges in processing complex, high-dimensional, and multimodal datasets. Emphasis will be placed on ensuring the trustworthiness , explainability, and security of AI applications to support real-world clinical decision-making.

A core mission of MLCare is to train a new generation of 14 interdisciplinary researchers with expertise spanning AI, computational biology, and healthcare . The program will equip doctoral candidates with the technical, analytical, and ethical skills needed to lead the future of patient-centered, AI-driven medicine. By combining state-of-the-art research with a comprehensive training program, MLCare aims to set new standards in personalized healthcare, ensuring equitable, data-driven solutions that improve outcomes across diverse populations. This project is poised to position Europe at the forefront of global innovation in precision medicine , delivering a timely and impactful response to evolving healthcare challenges.

The network’s science is carried by 15 connected PhD projects. Each is hosted by a different group, co-supervised across institutions, and linked to a partner. They are designed to feed one another: data and tools from one project become the inputs for several others.

Can a machine learn to recognize a real microprotein gene from its DNA alone? This project builds AI models that predict which short ORFs are genuinely translated, trained on data from across the network and released as open tools for the wider community.
Co-supervisor: Uwe Ohler (Max Delbrück Center, Berlin)

Can a machine learn to recognize a real microprotein gene from its DNA alone? Across the tree of life, genomes contain thousands of short open reading frames that might encode proteins, but most annotation tools were never designed to flag sequences this small. The result is that many genuine microprotein genes have been missed entirely.

This project builds a foundation model for smORF detection: an AI system that integrates mRNA sequence, cellular context, and ribosome profiling data to predict translation at codon-level resolution. The model learns from data across the ORFeus network, including dual host-pathogen datasets from DC4, rare translation events from DC3, and genetic variant information from DC12, and is iteratively refined as experimental validation comes in from groups across the consortium. The goal is not just a better predictor, but a set of open, reusable tools that the wider community can build on.
All models and predictions will be released through the ORFeome platform and HuggingFace. X
AI and machine learning, ribosome profiling data integration, cross-species computational genomics.
Reading translation one molecule at a time

What can single molecules tell us about translation that bulk methods cannot? This project combines single-molecule translation data with computational modeling to map which ORFs are translated from individual RNA isoforms, and how transcript structure and RNA modifications shape that choice.
Supervisor: Uwe Ohler (Max Delbrück Center, Berlin)

Standard ribosome profiling gives a population-level view: it tells you that a particular ORF is translated in a sample, but not which specific RNA molecule is being read, or how different transcript forms from the same gene carry different proteins. Many smORFs sit outside reference catalogs altogether, and some may be produced together from a single polycistronic transcript. This project goes beyond population averages to resolve translation at the level of individual RNA molecules and their isoforms.

The project builds on RiboSTAMP, a technique that marks translating ribosomes by fusing a cytidine deaminase to a ribosomal protein, combined with Oxford Nanopore long-read direct RNA sequencing to connect translation information directly to full-length transcript structure. The emphasis is computational: you will develop multi-omics methods that combine RiboSTAMP with ribosome profiling and polysome profiling to map translation onto specific RNA isoforms, and use RNA foundation models to quantify how RNA structure and modifications such as m6A shape which ORFs are translated. You will also help validate RiboSTAMP in the lab under normal and stress conditions, and test whether it can be adapted to single cells.

Results inform work across the network, from AI-based smORF prediction in DC1 and rare translation events in DC3 to RNA modification effects in DC7 and single-cell translation in DC9, and feed into the shared ORFeome resource. A secondment of around three months at Oxford Nanopore Technologies focuses on optimizing direct RNA sequencing and analysis workflows for RiboSTAMP.
Bioinformatics, Machine learning, Post-transcriptional gene regulation, Long-read sequencing, Genomics, Proteomics
